From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medivance.com>

Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional delete staging cadence & subprocessor certification

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're finalizing the DPA addendum and need one more clarification before procurement signs: how Redwood handles conditional delete for short-lived staging logs versus backups when a subprocessor is located in APAC.

Specifically:
- We want a separate cadence for staging logs (used for debugging) and persistent backups. Can you confirm whether you can:
  1) Set staging logs to a short TTL (<= 45 days) with automated safe-hold on investigation, and
  2) Keep backups for a maximum of 120 days but subject to a coordinated purge window (we prefer a 30-day grace quarantine before permanent deletion).

- Also, we need written confirmation that any APAC subprocessor (Trace Singh's team) maintains the signed subprocessors attestation and a current SOC2 (or equivalent) report. Can you attach the attestation and confirm whether subprocessor deletion hooks are available to trigger emergency rollbacks?

Attached: our draft DPA addendum (for your redline).

Can you get legal/ops eyes on this and reply with a proposed timeline? Procurement needs a committed schedule by EOD Thursday so we can target the next PO cycle.

Thanks,
Elena

--
Elena Morales
Head of Legal & Privacy, Medivance Health
elena.morales@medivance.com

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Laura (ops) to propose an operational schedule and confirm subprocessor attestations.

Quick answers up front: we can support separate cadences for staging vs backups, and we have emergency rollback hooks that can be tied to a joint incident playbook. Kimberly: could you advise on the DPA addendum redline and whether the emergency rollback clause needs any specific language around access logs? Laura: can ops outline a pragmatic purge cadence that meets Medivance's constraints?

I’ll follow up with a consolidated proposal by EOD Wednesday so you have it before procurement's Thursday deadline.

—Markus

Elena / Markus — legal reviewed the draft and have two items we want to lock before sign-off:

1) Subprocessor attestations: we can surface current attestations and a redacted SOC2 report for Trace Singh's team.
   - Action: Redwood will provide vendor-signed subprocessor attestation and a redacted SOC2 summary (we cannot share the full SOC2 without a mutual NDA addendum; summary will include scope, type II date, and gap remediation notes).

2) Retention windows & emergency rollback: propose the following operational language to include in the DPA addendum and procurement schedule:
   - Staging logs (debug/replica): TTL = 45 days; safe-hold requests can pause automated deletion for up to 30 days once invoked (subject to approval workflow).
   - Backup snapshots (persistent): TTL = 120 days; upon purge, snapshots move to a 30-day quarantine folder before irreversible deletion.
   - Emergency rollback: ops will support a documented rollback hook that can be executed within the quarantine window; rollback execution requires a joint authorization from Medivance Legal + Redwood Privacy (audit trail will be recorded).

We attach a proposed redline to the DPA addendum and a checklist of evidence items we will deliver. Please review and confirm whether the safe-hold durations are acceptable.

Attached: DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf (redline), vendor-soc2-report-2025.pdf (redacted summary).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Legal
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Kimberly — thanks, that covers most of it and the safe-hold wording looks reasonable. A few clarifications:

- Can Redwood commit to delivering the attestation and SOC2 redacted summary by EOD Friday? Procurement wants evidence with the signed PO.
- On the rollback authorization: our preference is joint sign-off from Medivance Security (not Legal) + Redwood Privacy. LegalOps looped in.
- One ask on quarantine: we prefer a technical safeguard that prevents automated purge until the quarantine period completes (i.e., a locked flag) rather than a time-based script only — is that implementable?

We will sign the addendum once we receive the attestation and redacted SOC2. Also starting the DocuSign flow now.

Elena

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Conditional delete staging cadence & subprocessor certification

Elena — appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and proposed schedule below (we can mirror this in the addendum):

1) Evidence delivery (by EOD Fri):
   - Redwood provides Trace's signed subprocessor attestation and a redacted SOC2 summary (see Kim's note).
   - Attached: staged-delete-schedule.xlsx (ops implementation plan).

2) Operational cadence (ops will implement the following):
   - Staging logs TTL: 45 days.
   - Safe-hold: once invoked via the joint incident channel, automated deletion is blocked (locked flag) for 30 days. Manual extension possible with mutual written approval.
   - Backup snapshots TTL: 120 days; upon scheduled purge, snapshots are moved to a quarantine bucket for 30 days where purging is blocked unless an authorized rollback is executed.
   - Rollback: can be executed during quarantine by joint authorization from Medivance Security + Redwood Privacy; all actions are logged and retained for 7 years for audit.

3) Implementation notes:
   - The locked-flag mechanism is implementable; ops will add a metadata lock on quarantine objects to prevent scripted deletion.
   - We will provide a one-time operational runbook and a 30-day test window after signing to validate rollback procedures.

4) Sign-off path:
   - Once attestation and SOC2 summary are posted, Elena to return the DocuSign signature. Redwood will post the redline as final in the DocuSign envelope and provide HubSpot record HS-98765 for the PO.

If this schedule looks good, we’ll attach the final addendum to the DocuSign envelope and push to procurement.

Thanks — Markus
